answer_text:
# 🇺🇦 Ukraine — Latest News (June 2026)

Here is a summary of the most recent developments regarding Ukraine and the ongoing war:

---

## ⚔️ Battlefield Situation

- Ukraine's ability to impede the flow of Russian supplies and personnel to the front lines has grown in recent days, from the southern regions of Zaporizhia and Kherson to the eastern front, forcing the Russian army to a standstill, according to battlefield analysis.

- General Oleksandr Komarenko reported that Ukrainian forces had restored control over **285.6 km²** in the Oleksandrivka direction. February 2026 became the first month since 2024 when Ukraine regained more territory than it lost.

- On May 31, Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps declared it had established fire control over the cities of Luhansk, Starobilsk, Alchevsk, Bryanka, and Kadiivka — all 50 to 90 km inside occupied Luhansk. It was the first time Ukraine declared such interdiction power over the eastern region.

---

## 🚀 Strikes & Attacks

- On June 2, Russia fired a mix of **656 drones and 73 missiles** into Ukrainian civilian areas, killing 23 people and injuring at least 130. Ukraine intercepted 91.7% of drones and 90.6% of cruise missiles, but only 27% of ballistic missiles.

- Ukraine has continued to strike refineries and munitions factories deep inside Russia, weakening its war effort.

- Multiple Storm Shadow missiles struck the **Kremniy EL factory** in Bryansk, described as one of Russia's largest military microelectronics producers.

---

## 🏛️ Political Developments

- Ukraine struck the city of **St. Petersburg** as Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived there for a high-profile economic forum, and President Zelenskyy wrote him an open letter telling him he could not win the war.

- **Kyrylo Budanov**, head of military intelligence (HUR), was appointed to replace Andriy Yermak as head of the **Office of the President of Ukraine**.

- President Zelenskyy dismissed the head of the **State Border Guard Service** and forced the head of the **SBU** (Security Service), Vasyl Malyuk, to resign.

---

## 📊 Casualties & Resources

- According to HUR director Oleh Ivashchenko and President Zelenskyy, a classified Kremlin assessment showed that approximately **1,315,000 Russian soldiers** had been killed.

- Russia produces **120 ballistic missiles a month**, Zelenskyy told the Ukraine-NATO Council — twice as many as the Patriot interceptors the United States produces.
